criteria.reasoning: The deliverable's results table gives the LYBUNT count as 11 households ("LYBUNT households ... **11**"), and the LYBUNT section lists 11 households and is headed "LYBUNT — 11 households". This matches the criterion's required count of 11.
The deliverable's results table gives the SYBUNT count as 9 households, and the SYBUNT section header and list both show 9 households. That matches the criterion's required count.

The deliverable reports 'Retention = 15 ÷ 22 = 68.2%'. It states the denominator as the 22 FY2025 households and the numerator as the 15 that gave again in FY2026, and lists the households in each group. This matches the criterion exactly, and I found no contradicting rate elsewhere in the report.

The LYBUNT table lists Dana Whitfield as #2, with the note "Northgate's $500 match of 2026-08-12 is the company's gift; she has only a soft credit for it." That matches the criterion. Her name does not appear anywhere in the deliverable as excluded from the LYBUNT list.

The LYBUNT table lists Gregory Szabo as #3 with a $100 gift on 2026-04-09, and notes that his $250 gift of 2026-07-20 was refunded on 2026-07-22, so it was not counted as an FY2027 gift. That meets the criterion.

The deliverable lists Marguerite Osei as LYBUNT #4 ($150, 2025-12-03). It also notes that the $400 given through her birthday fundraiser page in August 2026 is the givers' money and that she holds soft credits only. This meets the criterion.
The deliverable lists Celeste Moreau as #1 in the LYBUNT table with '$250, 2026-06-30' and the note 'June 30 is the last day of FY2026'. This is what the criterion requires.

The LYBUNT table of 11 households does not include any Achebe. The deliverable explicitly lists "the Achebes (Daniel, $300 on 2026-08-28)" under "Not LYBUNTs" because the household already gave in FY2027. That meets the criterion.

The LYBUNT table lists "Erik and Annika Lindqvist" once, at row 5, with the note "One household". The method section also says the Lindqvists' split joint checks count once. They are neither listed twice nor missing.

The LYBUNT table lists row 11 as 'Benjamin and Clara Hartwell | $2,500 from Clara, 2025-12-29', noting the household gave in FY2026. The SYBUNT table has nine households and Benjamin Hartwell is not among them. Both conditions of the criterion are met.

The SYBUNT table lists Lorraine Abernathy as #1 with the note "her FY2026 gift was refunded". She does not appear on the LYBUNT list. The method section also explains that the refunded $500 of 2026-04-16 was excluded.
The SYBUNT table lists Walter Pruitt as #2 with "$100, 2020-08-18" and fiscal year FY2021, inside the FY2021–FY2025 window, so he is treated as a SYBUNT, not lapsed.

The deliverable does not list Ingrid Solberg on either the LYBUNT or SYBUNT table. It says explicitly: "Not SYBUNTs: Ingrid Solberg — last gift 2020-05-02, FY2020, before the window, so she is lapsed." That matches the criterion's requirement.

The SYBUNT table lists '8 | Samir and Leila Haddad | $500 joint check, 2025-06-30 | FY2025' once, as one household. The LYBUNT list has no Haddad. Leila's spouse credit is excluded as a soft credit. The criterion is met.

The deliverable excludes all four organizations: "every organization — Northgate Systems, Thistlewood Family Foundation, Sourwood Garden Club and Ferncliff Brewing Co." None appears on the LYBUNT or SYBUNT tables. The retention numerator and denominator lists name only individual households. Northgate is mentioned only as the source of a soft-credit match, not as a counted entity.
